description: The Atlas Odyssey is a team interested in software, interactive experiences, and space exploration. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we want to create an engaging and educational solution that helps users understand the challenges of living and working on the Moon or Mars. We are especially interested in web development, game design, visualization, and creative problem-solving.
summary: AtlasHarvest is an interactive web application that helps farmers explore climate-smart crop rotation strategies using NASA POWER climate data. It combines historical rainfall and temperature observations with farm conditions, soil characteristics, and financial assumptions to compare crop rotations. The application includes climate visualizations, explainable recommendations, and financial risk scenarios to support better agricultural decisions.
details:
AtlasHarvest — Climate-Smart Farming with NASA Data

AtlasHarvest is an interactive web application developed by The Atlas Odyssey for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Field Shift challenge.

Problem: Farmers face unpredictable rainfall, drought, water shortages, and changing growing conditions. Choosing sustainable crop rotations requires understanding climate conditions, soil characteristics, and economic constraints.

Our Solution: AtlasHarvest integrates historical rainfall and temperature observations from NASA POWER with farmer-provided information to help users compare alternative crop-rotation strategies.

Main Features:

  • Interactive climate dashboard displaying historical rainfall and temperature statistics.
  • Geographic selection and farm configuration.
  • Comparison of four crop-rotation strategies.
  • Explainable scoring based on environmental and farming constraints.
  • Financial risk scenarios exploring budget sensitivity and drought conditions.
  • Interactive charts and downloadable analysis.

Technologies: Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, NASA POWER API, and data visualization tools. OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex assisted with development and design.

Innovation and Impact: AtlasHarvest combines NASA climate observations, agricultural decision support, and financial scenario analysis into an accessible platform focused initially on Morocco.

The prototype uses transparent, rule-based scoring and illustrative financial assumptions rather than an independently validated agricultural prediction model. It is designed to support exploration, not replace professional agronomic advice.
